notes: Which address ranges your container runtime may allocate, and which it must leave alone. Checked by 'db-ops control worker-status'; the rules are in db_ops/lib/network_policy.py.
This is the file db-ops init writes, not a sample: it is read as it stands. data/network_reservations.example.json carries worked examples of the parts that ship empty.

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Docker's default address pool is 172.17.0.0/16 through 172.31.0.0/16, handed out a /16 at a time. That is private RFC-1918 space, which is also where a great many estates put real servers. When a Docker bridge claims a range you route databases on, the host route table starts sending that traffic into the bridge: the database vanishes from that one host while staying reachable from everywhere else, and the collector reports an ordinary connect timeout. Nothing in the error says 'routing'.

'routed_ranges' ships EMPTY and must be filled in from your own inventory - it is the one list only you can write, and a range that is routed but not declared is a range this check cannot defend. Shipping a guess here would hard-code one estate's network into the product.

'container_ranges' ships with the two ranges db_ops pins for itself, because those are the product's own choice and match db_ops/sre/host_config/docker-daemon.json. Applying the confinement is a separate host-side step: copy that file to /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart Docker.

A container network outside every declared 'container_ranges' entry is reported UNCONFINED even when it collides with nothing today - because Docker, not you, chose that range, so the next network it creates is a coin flip. That finding fires while nothing is broken, which is the only moment the fix is free.

container_ranges.note: Where db_ops puts everything it names itself: docker0 (via the 'bip' setting in docker-daemon.json), its own runtime compose network, and the lab subnets derived per lab name by db_ops.sre.docker_db.models.lab_network_subnet. That derivation is what keeps a provisioned lab safe even on a host where docker-daemon.json was never applied.

Where 'default-address-pools' in docker-daemon.json confines every network nobody pinned, in /24 chunks. A compose project that declares no network lands here instead of in your servers' address space.
